title: HTML Introduction
summary: HTML labels the parts of a web page. Make a small page with a heading and a paragraph, then change the words yourself.
introduction: Have you ever made a poster for school? A web page can have a title, some sentences and pictures too. HTML tells the browser which part is which. A browser is an app, such as Chrome or Firefox, that shows web pages. Let us make a tiny page together.
learningObjectives: Explain how HTML labels a web page
Make a page with a heading and a paragraph
Find a tag, an element and an attribute

blocks.text: **HTML** stands for HyperText Markup Language. That is a long name for a simple idea: label the parts of a page. A label can say, "This is a heading" or "This is a paragraph." You do not need to learn the long name by heart.

Three tools often work together. HTML adds the words and page parts. [CSS](/tutorials/css) chooses colours and spaces. [JavaScript](/tutorials/javascript) can make things happen when you click. We will start with HTML.

blocks.title: A complete HTML page

items: `<!DOCTYPE html>` tells the browser to use today's HTML rules.
`<html>` holds the whole page. `lang="en"` says that its words are in English.
`<head>` holds facts about the page. `<title>` sets the words on the browser tab.
`<body>` holds the things people see on the page.

rows:

Hello!

` has two tags and the word inside.
An extra fact in a start tag. In `<html lang="en">`, `lang="en"` gives the page language.

questions.question: HTML decides which colour a heading should be.
questions.explanation: HTML labels the heading. CSS chooses how it looks, including its colour and size.

questions.question: In `<html lang="en">`, which part gives an extra fact about the page?
questions.explanation: `lang="en"` is an attribute. It tells the browser that the words on the page are in English.
